summary: Specifies a YANG data model for client and server implementations of the Two-Way Active Measurement Protocol (TWAMP). The model is also described with UML class diagrams, and it lets network management tools configure and monitor TWAMP. It is standards-track.

eli5.summary: TWAMP is a way to measure how fast messages travel across a network. This document gives a standard form that management software can use to set up and read the measuring tools.

questions: what is the twamp yang model
how to configure twamp with yang
subtitle: A standard YANG model so network tools can configure and monitor TWAMP measurements on any vendor's equipment.

tldr.problem: TWAMP measures network performance with probe packets, but implementations come with no standard management framework, so each vendor provides a proprietary way to configure them.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8913 describes the four TWAMP roles (Control-Client, Server, Session-Sender, Session-Reflector) with UML class diagrams and specifies a vendor-independent data model for them in YANG 1.1, compliant with the Network Management Datastore Architecture.
tldr.outcome: TWAMP can be configured and monitored across vendors through NETCONF or RESTCONF. Operational actions such as starting or stopping sessions and retrieving results are left to each implementation.

today: RFC 8913 is a Proposed Standard, published in November 2021. It has not been obsoleted or updated by a later RFC.

sections.title: Why TWAMP Needs a Data Model
sections.content:
The Two-Way Active Measurement Protocol (TWAMP, RFC 5357) measures network performance parameters such as latency, bandwidth and packet loss by sending probe packets and observing their experience in the network. To date, implementations have had no standard management framework, so implementers had to provide a proprietary mechanism.

That limits flexibility in large, virtualized and dynamically instantiated infrastructures, where measurements need to be set up across equipment from different vendors. The RFC points to two trends: large-scale, multi-vendor TWAMP deployments, and software-defined, virtualized networks that need a well-defined data model. A YANG data model (YANG 1.1, RFC 7950) fills that gap. It is compliant with the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA, RFC 8342).
sections.eli5: Every brand of stopwatch has its own odd buttons. This document makes all of them use the same buttons, so one person can run them all.

sections.title: Scope and the Logical Model
sections.content:
The goal is a vendor-independent data model for TWAMP implementations. It follows the TWAMP logical model: a Control-Client talks to a Server over TWAMP-Control, and a Session-Sender sends test packets to a Session-Reflector over TWAMP-Test. In a simplified model, one node acts as both Control-Client and Session-Sender and another acts as both Server and Session-Reflector. A configuration client then manages each node using, for instance, NETCONF (RFC 6241) or RESTCONF (RFC 8040).

The model is orthogonal to the protocol used to carry the configuration. It also does not cover operational actions: how test sessions are started and stopped, how results are retrieved, or how stored results are cleared. Those are not part of RFC 5357 and are out of scope. For measurement results, the Performance Metrics Registry (RFC 8911) can be used to develop a separate model.
sections.eli5: The model is like a wiring diagram for the four players in a race: the one who starts it, the one who watches, the runner and the one who bounces the baton back.

sections.title: The Four Roles and What Is Configured
sections.content:
The model holds four kinds of items: global settings per device (for example, the administrative status saying whether a node may act as Control-Client, Server or both), settings per TWAMP-Control connection (such as the Server IP address), settings per TWAMP-Test session (such as the DSCP value), and operational state.

  • Control-Client: an admin state, a mode-preference list, a key chain, and a list of control connections, each holding the test sessions to request. Each connection and session has a unique name, needed because details like TCP and UDP port numbers are not yet known when it is created.
  • Server: an admin state, the TCP port, timeouts, a key chain and the modes it offers. Its list of active control connections is read-only, and each connection is identified by the 4-tuple of client IP, client TCP port, server IP and server TCP port.
  • Session-Sender: one test session per outgoing TWAMP-Test session, with a packet count and a packet distribution that is either periodic or Poisson.
  • Session-Reflector: an admin state and the REFWAIT timeout, plus read-only data on each incoming test session.

A Server or Session-Reflector has no foreknowledge of incoming connections or sessions, so any parameter it wants to apply must be configured at the overall level and apply to all of them.
sections.eli5: The sender and the client choose their settings ahead of time. The ones on the receiving end cannot know who will show up, so they set one rule for everybody.

sections.title: Key Parameters and Behavior
sections.content:
The Control-Client keeps a mode-preference-chain, a list of modes with a 16-bit unsigned priority. Zero is the highest priority, and each increase of one lowers it. The Control-Client MUST choose the highest-priority mode that the Server Greeting offers. If it cannot determine an acceptable mode, or the bit combination makes no sense, it MUST respond with zero Mode bits set in the Set-Up-Response message to show it will not continue.

A key-chain maps each key-id to a secret-key. The Server and Control-Client use the same mapping, so key-id must be unique across the administrative domain. The secret key is a binary value that SHOULD contain at least 128 bits of entropy. The derived key length MUST be 16 octets for the AES session key and 32 octets for the HMAC-SHA1 session key.

The Server listens on server-tcp-port, which defaults to 862. The servwait timeout defaults to 900 seconds. The count and max-count-exponent values control how much key derivation work a Server may demand, which limits denial-of-service attacks.

On a Session-Reflector, each test session is indexed by a Session Identifier (sid) that the Server auto-allocates. A user who cannot reach the Control-Client can only retrieve all sessions from the reflector and pick out the ones of interest. Each reflector session also records its parent control connection 4-tuple, so it can be traced back to the connection that negotiated it.
sections.eli5: The client keeps a ranked wish list of secret handshakes and uses the best one the server knows. Both sides also keep matching secret-key notebooks.

sections.title: The YANG Module and Examples
sections.content:
The formal definition is the YANG module ietf-twamp, with namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-twamp. Its top-level twamp container holds client, server, session-sender and session-reflector subtrees, each guarded by a feature of the same name. Data that is read-only is marked as operational state.

The module imports common types from RFC 6991 and references the TWAMP specification and its extensions, including mixed security mode (RFC 5618), individual session control (RFC 5938), reflect octets and symmetrical size (RFC 6038) and the IKEv2-derived key feature (RFC 7717). Section 6 and Appendix A give examples of data that conform to the module for each of the four roles.
sections.eli5: The module is the official rulebook written in a language that computers can read, with worked examples so people can check they understood it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Virtually all existing TWAMP measurement systems are administered by a single network operator. Attackers could try to commandeer the packet generation capability or corrupt measurements. The model is accessed through NETCONF, whose mandatory-to-implement secure transport is SSH, or RESTCONF, whose mandatory transport is TLS. The Network Configuration Access Control Model (RFC 8341) can restrict users to a subset of operations and content.

Several writable nodes are sensitive. Writing admin-state can cause unintended test sessions. A large number-of-packets can make a session run longer than expected. The REFWAIT, count and max-count-exponent values can tie up resources, since the latter two drive PBKDF2 iterations. A changed DSCP marking can skew test traffic and manipulate results. Changing mode-preference-chain can force unauthenticated or unencrypted traffic, enabling an on-path attack.

The readable token node, a concatenation of a challenge, an AES session key and an HMAC-SHA1 session key, is sensitive and can be used to disrupt a test session, so read access should be limited to the test network administrator.
sections.eli5: The remote control must be kept away from strangers. Someone who presses the wrong buttons could start races nobody wanted, slow them down, or turn off the lock on the secret handshake.

sections.title: Operational Commands Left Out
sections.content: Appendix B explains that operational commands could be performed programmatically or through a command-line interface. In principle YANG could define NETCONF remote procedure calls for starting or stopping control connections and test sessions, retrieving results or clearing stored results. Because RFC 5357 does not describe such actions, and implementations may support different sets of commands with different restrictions, the document leaves it to each implementation to define its own data model for them.
sections.eli5: The standard covers the settings dial but not the start and stop buttons. Each maker adds those buttons their own way.
